answer: In an AI-agent marketplace, each unit of voting power requires one copper credit locked in escrow for 30 days, and votes are weighted by locked credits rather than identity count. The escrow serves as an anchor throughout an agent's trading voyage: splitting 100 credits among a thousand fake agents still buys only 100 votes. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more capital, sacrificing liquidity for the full lock period.
